content.comment_body: I am considering using the [product_name] to control a proportional valve. I have the [product_name] equipped with an [product_name] expansion module, and the program is operational. Unexpectedly, it turns out we now need to control a 2-position proportional valve using a -10V to +10V signal, but my setup only provides 0-10V output. Does anyone have a suggestion for addressing this issue?

Hello [user_name], There are several potential solutions, and you’ll need to choose the most cost-effective one for your situation. First option: Consider using a signal converter that converts 0-10V input to -10V to +10V output. I found something online that handles a 4-20mA input and produces -10V to +10V output, which would mean you first have to convert your signal to 4-20mA—adding to both complexity and cost. Second option: Use two separate relays—activate the first relay when supplying the valve in the 0-10V range, and the second when you need the -10V to 0V range. Note that this approach has a major drawback: the switching time between relays may temporarily interrupt the signal to your valve, for example, when decreasing from 1V to -1.3V, there could be a gap between de-energizing one relay and activating the other, which would leave the valve without a signal during that transition.

The current setup provides only a 0-10V output, which falls short of the required range. Community suggestions center around either signal conversion hardware, which may increase costs and complexity, or relay-based solutions that could introduce signal interruptions.
